title: Candidate
description: One Technical Credit claim made by one rule, with its evidence. Every rule outputs exactly this shape. FROZEN since Nov 11: do not change without the whole team agreeing. This file matches src/tc_detector/contracts/candidate.py. The Python code also checks one thing JSON Schema can't: that id was built from the other fields.

id.description: Unique name for this finding, used to match it with a human label. Built as repo:service:file:location:pattern, where location is 'start-end' for line ranges or the word 'file' / 'service', and a missing file is written '-'. Example: petclinic:api-gateway:src/GatewayConfig.java:12-40:gateway

repo.description: Which target repo was scanned, e.g. 'petclinic'. No ':' allowed, because ':' separates the parts of the id.

commit.description: The exact git commit that was scanned. Code changes over time, so results only make sense at a fixed commit.

service.description: Which microservice the evidence is in, e.g. 'api-gateway'. No ':' allowed (id separator).

file.description: Path to the evidence file, relative to the service root and using '/'. Example: 'src/main/resources/logback-spring.xml'. Not allowed: a leading '/', '\', ':' or '..', so each file can only be written one way. May be null only when unit is 'service'.

line_start.description: First line of the evidence, counting from 1. Required for unit 'line_range'; must be null for 'file' and 'service', since a fake range would break matching.

line_end.description: Last line of the evidence (same as line_start for a single line). Same null rules as line_start. The Python code also checks line_end >= line_start.

unit.description: How precise the claim is, which decides how it is matched to labels: 'line_range' = these exact lines, 'file' = this whole file, 'service' = this whole service.

pattern.description: What kind of credit this is, in lowercase words joined by dashes, e.g. 'tracing-span' or 'gateway'.

category.description: Which of the six Technical Credit categories from the course spec this belongs to. Used to group results in the report.

rule_id.description: Which rule produced this, so each rule's accuracy can be measured. Format: category-name-NN, e.g. 'observability-tracing-01'. Must start with this candidate's own category (checked below).

snippet.description: The evidence text that Claude reads to confirm or reject the claim. Capped at 2000 characters because we pay for every character sent to Claude.

allOf.description: A line_range claim needs a file and both line numbers. Any other unit must have null line numbers.
A file claim must say which file.
This block and the five after it (one per category): rule_id must start with its category, which catches copy-paste mistakes.
